_comment: The corpus for #131, pinned. Every engine reads the same flat `.sup`, so no demux
difference can contaminate a comparison, and every scored item names the exact
sidecar it is scored against with that file's SHA-256.
The sidecar was chosen ONCE, by one engine (`subtrackt-arial`), before any other
engine ran, and then frozen. `scripts/accuracy/analyse.py` picks the best-agreeing
sidecar per title; that rule is correct there and would be poison here, because
applied per engine it lets each engine be scored against whichever transcript
flatters it most. The `candidates` list records what the selector saw, and the
spread between its entries is the instrument's own uncertainty on that title: an
inter-engine gap smaller than that spread is not a result.
kind: `scored` yields CER/WER. `smoke` claims no accuracy and asserts only that the
track survives its own shape. `arithmetic` is measured for cost and multiplied.
cost: the item is REPEATED, and is the only kind of item a timing figure may come
from. #209 widened this corpus from 6 items to 26, 24 of them scored, and paid for
it by dropping to one run each -- which the first run's own results licensed: all
64 (engine, item)
pairs were byte-identical across three repeats, so every accuracy figure published
was the median of three identical numbers. Timing is the exception and it is not a
small one -- `pgstosrt` read 254.8 / 67.5 / 67.3 s on `deathrace2`, a 278% spread,
with CPU-seconds moving with it (996 against 266), which is a four-fold difference
in work done rather than stopwatch noise. So five items stay repeated and every
wall, CPU, %CPU and RSS figure in `docs/alternatives.md` is drawn from those five.
`bighero6` is one of them despite claiming no accuracy: it is carried for cost, and
the sovereign#328 cross-check is the reason it is in the corpus at all.
Titles after the original six are drawn by `select.py` from the fifty-title library
sample, in `scripts/accuracy/sample.py`'s hash-of-folder order so the draw
re-derives rather than being hand-picked. NOT from the 21 titles the sidecar
corroborates: that restriction is circular, since it selects titles by the outcome
being measured, and `docs/library-accuracy.md` says so in those words.
The draw walked 40 records to find 20. Seventeen were rejected because their best
sidecar does not transcribe what the track does, three had no scoreable sidecar at
all, and `select.py` prints every one with its reason. Two rejections are worth
knowing about because neither cue pairing nor sound-cue counts can see them: the
*Insomnia* case, where a sidecar of the same convention comes from a different
release, pairs by timing and shares almost no words -- 1,213 extracted cues against
a 1,974-cue sidecar in block capitals, reading 77.2%. Those are caught by the
confident-read test, which is `docs/library-accuracy.md`'s own measurement made into
a rule and fires only when the matcher says it read the glyphs. A title the
reference set fits badly is kept however badly it scores: `excision` is here at
22.9% selector CER on a fit of 30.5.

items.note: Generated by `xtask make-fixture --repeat 50`. The only corpus item with true ground truth, and therefore the only certifiable absolute CER in the comparison. Scored against `synthetic.srt`, which #131 added so one instrument scores every row.

The tuned baseline; a marked italic act at 6% of characters. The plain sidecar is the selector's choice by a wide margin -- the disc track is dialogue-only and the SDH sidecar carries 1,057 cues against the track's 822.

The third Arial title. SDH, and the SDH sidecar is the match: the track carries 85 bracketed sound cues the plain sidecar has none of, which #175 measured as more than half of its apparent error. 1,396 cues on both sides exactly.

The long end of the library; 18% of lines lean and the release marks none of them. The widest sidecar spread in the corpus by far: the Blu-ray sidecar pairs 2,442 cues against 2,442 and reads 1.4%, the WEB-DL SDH one reads 51.8%. Two releases, not two conventions.

sovereign#328's title, carried for cost rather than for accuracy -- without it the cross-comparison against that analysis is title-to-title rather than like-for-like. Its 1,745 bitmaps reproduce #328's count exactly. SMOKE, not scored, and the reason is the roster's own rule: the disc track is SDH -- "(WHISTLING)", "MAN:" -- and the one English sidecar in the folder is plain dialogue carrying none of it, 1,324 cues against the track's 1,745. The selector read 22.8% against it, which is a measure of the mismatch and not of any engine. #131 assumed this row had "no sidecar spread"; it is worse than that -- the single sidecar does not match, so scoring it would put false entries in the column the bench tells you to read.
One track of the 37 #328 projected at 8.4 hours. Measured once and multiplied; no accuracy claimed and none scored.
